correctness.rationale: For n>=3, strict convex-cyclic side-length chambers separate into centered (all signs +) and noncentered (only the unique longest side negative); the diameter/semicyclic locus is excluded. Differentiate signed central-angle closure and the signed fan-area formula to obtain R_j=R sigma_j/(q_j S), gradient A_i=sigma_i q_i/2 and H=diag(-sigma_i d_i/(2q_i))+(2R^2/S)vv^T with v_i=sigma_i/q_i. On centered chambers D negative and the update positive; on noncentered D has positive index 1 while the update is negative. In both cases rank-one inertia implies <=1 positive eigenvalue; Euler homogeneity d^T H d=2Area>0 gives at least one. Determinant lemma with 4R^2 T-S=sum sigma_i q_i/d_i>0 proves H nonsingular. Hence exactly (1,n-1) for every stated chamber. A harmless but genuine intermediate typo in the source proof writes S=2R sum tan(alpha) (twice); by definitions S=sum tan(alpha), and only its sign is invoked, so the displayed final Hessian and inertia proof remain correct. Independent central-angle finite-difference checks cover both chambers but are not a universal proof.
risks: The source proof mistakenly multiplies S by 2R in one intermediate tangent identity; it is dimensionally inconsistent but used only for the sign. No claim on semicyclic or degenerate boundaries; numerical checks cannot replace the analytic proof.
